facts.text: Single rack of small to #3 cams is enough; the short summit offwidth needs no #4 (July)
Keep the pack small or tow it: three squeeze chimneys on a wandering line are awkward with a bulky bag (July).
In early September the usual way down is the west ridge: a few rappels and down-scrambling along a narrow crest, then a loose gully of sand and rubble that runs fast underfoot.
Sandy rubble in the lower west-side descent gully (early September) sends rocks down on partners below

facts.text: Loose gully of sand over big blocks leads to the notch; rockfall is easy to trigger (early October)
Rappel chains sit mid-route; a running belay across the exposed crest to the notch below the final pitch is enough (September).
Rappelling from the summit: the second set of chains lands on poor ground, so use the boulder anchor below it to reach flat ground just west of the north-ridge notch ledge (September).

notes: Every harvested track starts roughly 200 m from the Complete South Buttress trailhead pin but 320-575 m from the pins on the other routes, so those pins are probably a few hundred metres off (tracks start near 48.5134,-120.6879). I tried OpenStreetMap and the summitpost page and could not confirm the coordinate, so no move is proposed. The Cauthorn-Wilson and East Face routes share identical pins and approach text and may be misfiled copies of each other. The South Buttress and West Ridge assignments would fail the 300 m start rule until a trailhead pin is confirmed.
